minutes.headline: Committee suspended the unpaid school lunch balance policy through the closure and heard the remote learning plan.
minutes.summary: A Saturday remote meeting during the COVID-19 school closure. The committee voted by roll call to suspend the unpaid meal balance notice policy until the closures end, and heard the superintendent, special education director and social worker explain the move from enrichment to remote learning. The business manager gave preliminary cost updates and said the FY21 budget will be revised after town guidance. The meeting adjourned by roll call.

public_comment.topic: Chair checked for public comment on agenda items; none offered by members or online viewers.
A resident asked whether food service and extended day cost figures were compared to budget, and about tracking additional COVID costs.
Asked for a public ledger of COVID costs and reimbursements, for analysis of keeping paychecks versus unemployment for hourly staff, and for consolidated student/parent policies.
Said they contacted the state senator about cancelling MCAS and noted federal waivers.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted 5-0 by roll call to suspend the unpaid meal balance policy until the school closure ends.
The business manager gave preliminary cost projections for meals, cafeteria wages and extended day, and said the FY21 budget will be revised after town guidance.
The purchasing freeze (except health, safety, meals and online learning) and the hiring freeze continue.
The superintendent, special education director and social worker explained the move from enrichment to remote learning.
A meeting is to be scheduled for the coming Wednesday evening to discuss April vacation, with a superintendent recommendation.

why_it_matters: Families with unpaid school meal balances will not get notices while schools are closed, and the cost of the meal program may fall partly on the local budget, which is mostly taxes, if federal reimbursement does not cover it.
The FY21 school budget is to be revised after town and state numbers are known, so the spending plan residents see later may differ from the earlier one.
